chapters:
Under the Hives
    - Maeve spots the limping cottontail bedding beneath the hottest hive row, starts slipping romaine after dark, rationalizes “only until it heals.” Close third with her stash in the warm room; tiny rabbit-sense interlude of thrum, dust coolness, botfly itch.

Electric Lines
    - Eli runs mite washes, notes cash flow in his spiral, beefs up the fencer with bacon-greased foil; Mara from the co-op pushes for fall promos he can’t quite promise. He smells something off near the pallets but can’t place it. Soot noses cappings; Ruth warns about “softness.”

The Post
    - Aiden films a dusk reel: rabbit under the hive, golden combs in frame. Views tick up; strangers arrive with carrot tops. Maeve flushes, pockets wrappers. Rabbit-sense: drone of tires, foot-vibration, heat-scent of greens. Eli confronts Aiden; Maeve stays quiet.

Lines on Paper
    - Warden Gary leaves a written warning about feeding wildlife and fence compliance; points out bear sign and spilled attractants. Henry Pike waves chewed kale and sets traps along the hedgerow, jabbing at an old pallet grudge. Eli’s tendon flares during a heavy pull; he tallies losses they can’t afford.

Hemostats
    - Maeve calls Lila. Night visit by headlamp: botfly warble removed, wound flushed; firm lecture on no feeding, brush cover instead. Maeve promises habitat, not handouts. Rabbit-sense: sharp metal taste, pressure-release, new coolness. For two nights, Maeve holds the line.

Break
    - Soot flushes at dusk when Aiden’s drone zips low; rabbit panics, snags the old fence scar, bolts to the powerline cut. Maeve relapses—parsley tucked under a block. That night a young bear tests the fence, pops a corner post, knocks two lids askew. Honey loss, brood chilled. Eli smells greens on the pallet boards. Ruth arrives with a casserole and the story of the dog her husband shot; the room goes quiet.

Confession Weather
    - First cold snap forecast, co-op threatens to shift shelf space if deliveries falter. Eli and Maeve fight; Maeve finally admits to feeding. He sleeps in his boots by the door; she sits in the warm room deleting rehab blog tabs, holding the cracked taillight lens like a worry stone. Rabbit-sense: the block wall’s stored heat thinning.

Brush, Not Bread
    - They choose a third path: with Lila’s guidance they build dense brush cover along the hedgerow and at the powerline edge; clean every attractant, move cappings indoors, tighten hot wires, hang bacon foil only at corners, schedule Henry to pull traps. Gary reinspects and signs off. Maeve texts Aiden to bench the drone and helps him post a “look, don’t lure” PSA. Rabbit resettles into the new cover, visits the hive shade at midday only.

The Pull and the Passage
    - Final honey pull under thin frost. A last bear test meets a crackle of clean fence and leaves only turned leaves. Co-op accepts a smaller, steady allotment with a “bear-safe” card. Ruth quietly pays the diesel bill again but says nothing. Eli’s ledger still tight yet balanced. Maeve walks the corridor at dawn: a tuft of fur caught on multiflora, fresh zig-zag tracks disappearing toward the powerline cut. Rabbit-sense: frost-tingled whiskers, distant thrum, dry seed scent. They stand at the fence, hands not quite touching, and let the space hold.
